Date: 2027-04-05T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightMarket latency spike — triage notes and suggested mitigation

Ben —

Preliminary triage (logs attached to internal drive link):
- Root cause: an autoscaler deadlock triggered by concurrent scale-up requests to the reserved pool control plane combined with an edge case in the warm-standby attach path. This produced stalled placement and a transient queue build-up on a subset of nodes.
- Impact window: ~07:43–08:20 PST (saw spike in 503s and P95).
- Mitigation performed at 08:22 PST: triggered targeted allocator restart for BrightMarket’s pool and disabled the concurrent attach path temporarily. Warm-standby instances were forced to reattach cleanly.
- Current state: tail latency stabilized by 08:30 PST and error rates returned to baseline by 08:35 PST. We put a temporary guard in place to reject concurrent attach ops for affected pools.

Next steps (recommended customer message):
- Provide an incident timeline and confirm the stabilization window.
- Offer a billing credit proportional to the committed-usage minutes impacted (rough estimate attached).
- Schedule a postmortem call with BrightMarket to review long-term fixes (kernel selector change + autoscaler throttling logic).

I’ve uploaded an internal incident_timeline.pdf with the detailed timeline and raw allocator traces to the drive link.

-Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

[Attachment: internal incident_timeline.pdf (internal link only)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-04-06T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Incident update and proposed credit for 2027-04-05 reserved pool impact

Samantha —

Thanks again for flagging this. Below is an interim summary and our proposed next steps. I’ve attached a customer-friendly incident timeline and an export of your usage for the impacted window.

Summary:
- What happened: an internal autoscaler race condition briefly stalled allocation for a subset of nodes in your reserved GPU pool, causing a small increase in 503s and elevated P95 for ~37 minutes (07:43–08:20 PST on 2027-04-05).
- What we did: targeted allocator restart, disabled concurrent attach path, and confirmed warm-standby reattachment. Tail latency returned to baseline by 08:35 PST.
- Current status: service stable and autoscaler throttles patched to prevent the concurrent-attach edge case. We will deploy a kernel-selection fix in the next weekly rollout.

Proposed commercial remediation:
- We propose a one-time billing credit equal to 5% of the daily committed fee for the affected day, pending confirmation of precise usage minutes. This is intended as a pause-the-billing goodwill gesture while we complete the postmortem.
- If you require a formal SLA credit calculation and legal letter, we’ll coordinate with our legal and finance teams and deliver a formal statement within 5 business days.

Suggested next steps:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether the proposed 5% credit is acceptable as an interim good-faith offer.
2) If procurement prefers a formal SLA credit calculation, loop in your contracts/legal and we’ll start the paperwork (we’ve cc’d procurement).
3) We recommend a 60-minute postmortem call next week to walk through the timeline and permanent fixes — I can coordinate times.

Attachments: incident_timeline.pdf (customer copy), usage_export.csv (request_log filtered 07:30–09:00 PST)

Apologies for the disruption — we take committed capacity incidents seriously and will share a full postmortem once complete.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0187
